title: PSA: Amazon’s shopping AI can now tell you if that message is a scam
description: Amazon is adding a scam-detection feature to Alexa for Shopping that can verify whether suspicious emails, texts, and other messages actually came from the retailer.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Adobe acquires Indian market intelligence startup Rilo
description: This is Adobe's second acquisition out of India after Rephrase.ai in 2023
author: Ivan Mehta

title: OpenAI faces 30 more lawsuits tied to Tumbler Ridge shooting
description: Edelson PC is filing 30 new lawsuits against OpenAI over the Tumbler Ridge shooting, escalating claims to aiding and abetting and naming Chris Lehane, though evidence remains unconfirmed.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: AfterQuery reportedly becomes Y Combinator’s fastest-ever unicorn, now valued at $3.2B
description: AI model-training startup AfterQuery has reportedly raised a round that valued it at $3.2 billion, just five months after announcing its $30 million Series A at a $300 million valuation in April.
author: Julie Bort

title: Open AI’s Astra model is on the way — and very good at breaking into computer systems
description: OpenAI previewed the precautions it is taking as it prepares to release Astra, its newest, cyber-critical LLM.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Google’s Android update tackles motion sickness, accessibility, and more
description: While some of the features see Google playing catch-up to Apple, which already offers similar features for iPhone users, others specifically leverage Gemini to provide various improvements.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: Anthropic’s new Fable release is cheaper, less restrictive
description: Fable 5.1 includes changes meant to reduce token cost and false-positive restrictions from the model's safeguards.
author: Russell Brandom

title: Google’s answer to Canva is an AI tool where you prompt instead of design
description: With Google Pics, Google is pushing deeper into the creative software market dominated by Canva and Adobe, but with a distinctly AI-first approach.
author: Sarah Perez

title: ChatGPT Health adds Epic integration for clinicians to import patient data
description: OpenAI said that the integration provides read-only access to health records for clinicians.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: Sequoia-incubated Empirik launches with $21M to predict outages before they happen
description: The startup wants to do for IT infrastructure what Cursor did for software engineering.
author: Marina Temkin

title: Amazon Alexa can now alert you when something new might tempt you to shop
description: Amazon is adding a new Alexa-powered feature called “Update Me When” that can send personalized alerts about product launches, tours, books, shows, and other events that could trigger a purchase.
author: Sarah Perez

title: AIR raises $50M to help companies vet the skills and add-ons AI agents use
description: AIR's platform can discover agents running at a company, continuously vets any skills and add-ons they use, and blocks any unwanted behavior.
author: Ram Iyer

title: Fambot introduces an ‘AI chief of staff’ for families
description: Fambot is building an AI “chief of staff” to help families manage the emails, calendars, school updates, sports schedules, and other logistics of raising kids.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Apple shares ‘shocking evidence’ against former employee accused of stealing company data for OpenAI
description: Apple says it has evidence that a former employee destroyed evidence of data theft after learning he was under investigation.
author: Amanda Silberling

title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok
description: Versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT and SpaceXAI's Grok will join Google's Gemini on the Pentagon's central portal for AI tools.
author: Kirsten Korosec

title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles
description: As frustration over AI influencers has been growing, Instagram is limiting the reach of undisclosed AI profiles.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: Harvard Law dropout raises $6M for Blue Voice to build a ‘Harvey for police officers’
description: Blue Voice is trained on department-specific laws, local ordinances, protocols, and guidelines that general-purpose AI tools can't access on the public internet.
author: Marina Temkin

title: Clipto uses AI to search terabytes of video and is now valued at $250M
description: The three-year-old startup says it reached $15 million in ARR and profitability before raising its latest $15 million round.
author: Kate Park

title: Nvidia’s $3.5B MediaTek bet reveals its plan for tackling Big Tech’s AI chip buildout
description: Nvidia invests $3.5 billion into Taiwanese chipmaker MediaTek. The deal shows how Nvidia plans to stay essential to AI infrastructure as Big Tech begins to build its own AI chips.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Meeting note-taker Circleback adds a free tier to attract more customers
description: Circleback is also introducing new pricing plans starting from $14 per month.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: The US is building barriers around drones and robots, but China has scale to get around them
description: The U.S. is shutting out more foreign-made drones and robots. China’s scale means the global competition may simply move elsewhere.
author: Kate Park

title: Musk’s faster path to more gas turbines comes with pollution problem
description: Elon Musk says a secretive new SpaceX foundry will let him cast his own turbine blades and get gas power online 18 months faster than anyone else — but it's a bet on a fuel source that's already triggering lawsuits and health studies everywhere his (and others') turbines have gone in.
author: Connie Loizos

title: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining
description: Caterpillar has spent decades putting autonomous machines to work at remote mining sites. It's now bringing that experience to AI deployment.
author: Kate Park

title: Sony Music, Warner sue Anthropic, alleging a “brazen campaign” of intellectual property theft
description: This latest lawsuit is particularly broad and homes in on accusations of illegal piracy.
author: Kirsten Korosec

title: At TechBBQ, Europe’s AI conversations kept coming back to: Who’s actually in control?
description: Investors, founders, and operators from across Europe arrived for the annual Nordic TechBBQ conference to talk about how humans can have agency over AI.
author: Dominic-Madori Davis

title: “We’re not doing 30 bets a year”: Vijay Pande on betting small after running $4 billion at a16z
description: Vijay Pande — who left a16z's roughly $4 billion biotech practice last year to start the much smaller, AI-native VZVC — talks about why biology is finally shifting from a "discovery" science to an "engineering" one, why clinical trials are still brutally expensive, and why he thinks open, shared datasets (not walled-off ones) are what will actually let AI transform medicine.
author: Connie Loizos

title: Nvidia’s AI advantage is moving beyond the GPU
description: The new generation of data center systems is increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles.
author: Russell Brandom

title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips
description: Neocloud Lambda has raised $1B in private debt to buy Nvidia AI chips and lease them to Microsoft. It's the latest in a string of loans, underscoring the high cost of the AI boom.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI
description: Given 10 benchmarks for specific misaligned behaviors, the automated systems were able to improve performance on every single one without degrading overall performance.
author: Russell Brandom

title: Open-weight AI companies are the Valley’s hottest acquisition targets
description: There's a lot of capital pouring into the business of giving models away.
author: Tim Fernholz
